sections.title: About Egypt
sections.content: Egypt is a country located in North Africa, rich in history and culture. Its public holidays commemorate national milestones, religious observances, and cultural traditions.

sections.title: How Public Holidays Affect Daily Life in Egypt
sections.content:
On most public holidays, government offices and public schools are closed, while banks and some businesses operate on reduced hours. Travel activity tends to increase significantly during major festive seasons.

Private businesses may choose whether or not to operate, often depending on company policy.

sections.title: Why Knowing Egypt's Public Holidays Matters
sections.content: Accurate holiday information helps with business planning, payroll management, and academic scheduling. It is also crucial for travel and accommodation planning to avoid delays in official or financial processes.

q.en: Are all public holidays observed nationwide in Egypt?

a.en: While many holidays are national, some observances may be limited to specific regions, states, or territories.

q.en: Do businesses and stores close on public holidays in Egypt?

a.en: Generally yes. Government offices, banks, and schools are closed. Essential services and some retail sectors may remain open or operate on reduced hours.

q.en: What happens if a public holiday falls on a weekend in Egypt?

a.en: In many cases, if a national holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the observance is moved to the following Monday, though this depends on specific local laws and the holiday in question.

q.en: Are public transport services affected by holidays in Egypt?

a.en: Yes, public transportation often runs on a reduced Sunday or holiday schedule during national public holidays.

q.en: Are employees entitled to paid time off on public holidays in Egypt?

a.en: Most full-time employees are legally entitled to a paid day off on national public holidays. Those who are required to work are typically eligible for premium pay or a substitute day off.
